name: Ballari (incl. Vijayanagara)
headline: A tracking drive found 259 out-of-school children but brought back only 38.
summary: In a drive reported in January 2025, officials identified 259 out-of-school children in Ballari but brought only 38 back to school. The deep-research report's claims about mining, poverty and mass weddings rested on a social-media post and a statewide article that does not name Ballari, so they are not used here.

reasons.detail: A tracking drive identified 259 out-of-school children but managed to bring only 38 back to class.

In 2020 a Ballari child rights commission member said most schools in the district only ran classes 6-8 and higher classes were elsewhere, away from hostels; girls dropped out and parents hesitated over distance.

Ballari had 395 vacancies among 1,014 sanctioned government high school posts in 2025, worst in Siruguppa (157 of 269) and Sandur (92 of 181); guest teachers covered 434 posts, with maths and science gaps.

Ballari ranked 29th in 2025 with 60 government high schools below 40% pass; in June 2024 the CM sought suspension of Vijayanagara's education officers after its education ranking fell from 10th to 27th.

State-level 2018-19 survey, where Ballari recorded 5,132 out-of-school children, cited migration, disinterest, domestic work, distance and parental reluctance to educate girls. Not broken out for Ballari.

headlines.takeaway: Child rights commission chair said Ballari had 2,018 children leaving school, the state's highest, and announced a readmission campaign.

responses.text: Ballari DDPI is preparing a plan with holiday special classes, show-cause notices for schools under 40% pass, and head teacher transfers; existing efforts include Kalika Aasare and phone-in programmes.
The state child rights commission's Shaale Kade Nanna Nade campaign (2016) aimed to readmit school leavers, citing Ballari's 2,018 as the state's highest.
